articles.title_zh: Court casts heavy doubt over most serious Netanyahu charges, in huge blow to prosecution
articles.content_orig:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s yearslong corruption trial took a significant turn in his favor on Wednesday as judges recommended that prosecutors drop charges in the most serious of the three cases against him and reconsider a second case.
In televised remarks later Wednesday, Netanyahu said the recommendations amount to a vindication and declared, “This trial needs to end immediately.”
Speaking at the Israeli parliament, or Knesset, the prime minister said: “It took 10 years of terrible suffering for me, my wife and my sons for the truth to finally be revealed to everyone. Who will give us back those years, during which my sons couldn’t go out to a restaurant or walk around the city?”
Netanyahu’s political allies also immediately celebrated the decision. “After years of persecution against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the time has come to put an end to a trial that was tainted from the outset, divides Israeli society, and exacts a heavy price from the country,” Defense Minister Israel Katz, a Netanyahu ally, said in a statement on X.
Judge Rivka Friedman-Feldman, who is presiding over the trial of Israel’s longest-serving leader, indicated to Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara in a hearing that a conviction of Netanyahu in what’s known as Case 4000 is unlikely and the case should be dropped.
“It seems to us that the bribery charge presents considerable difficulties,” the court said, according to a spokesperson. “There is serious doubt as to whether the evidentiary foundation supports this allegation.”
Trump pens letter asking Israeli president to pardon Netanyahu in corruption trial
In this case, prosecutors alleged that Netanyahu gave regulatory benefits worth more than 1 billion shekels (approximately $300 million) to his friend, millionaire Shaul Elovitch, whose telecommunications company Bezeq owned the Walla! news website.
Netanyahu faced a charge of bribery and another charge of fraud and breach of trust in this case.
The court emphasized that its recommendations in these cases were not final decisions or a judgment in the corruption trial, but the statements alone are nevertheless an enormous win for Netanyahu.
In his remarks in response to the recommendations, Netanyahu repeated Wednesday that he is prepared to form a unity government with the parliamentary opposition. Netanyahu’s political rival, Gadi Eisenkot, is maneuvering to form a government that would oust the prime minister and his far-right partners after nearly four years in power.
Justice Minister Yariv Levin shared one of Netanyahu’s old social media posts in which he said, “There will be nothing because there is nothing,” which became one of Netanyahu’s catchphrases when the cases began.
Baharav-Miara, who does not normally attend the trial, was summoned by the court to attend Wednesday’s hearing. The attorney general said she would “carefully review” all of the court’s recommendations with the prosecution team.
“There are only two ways to bring the case to a conclusion: a verdict or an appropriate plea agreement that reflects the nature of the acts and offenses,” she said during the hearing.
The court also recommended reconsidering Case 2000, in which prosecutors had alleged that Netanyahu sought favorable coverage in one of Israel’s top newspapers in exchange for limiting the circulation of one of that paper’s main rivals. Netanyahu faced the charge of fraud and breach of trust in this case.
“We have serious doubts as to whether the conduct described in the indictment actually constitutes a criminal offense,” the court said bluntly.
In the final case, known as Case 1000, the court urged Netanyahu’s attorneys to come to an agreement with prosecutors. In this case, Netanyahu is charged with fraud and breach of trust over allegations that he received gifts such as cigars and champagne from overseas businessmen. But this case was viewed as far less serious than Case 4000, and it would be a major political victory for Netanyahu if it’s the only one left standing.
The court said it seemed that Case 1000 could be “brought to a conclusion.”
Netanyahu was indicted in Jerusalem District Court in January 2020. At the time of the announcement, he was in the US visiting President Donald Trump during his first term. Hours after the indictment came down, Trump unveiled what would become known as his “Deal of the Century” to solve the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.
The indictment made Netanyahu the first sitting Israeli prime minister to appear in court as a defendant. The criminal trial, which began in May 2020, has lasted through several wars, multiple elections and two US presidents. Netanyahu began testifying in the trials in December 2024.
President Trump has asked Israeli President Isaac Herzog to pardon Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in his corruption trial. Will Herzog do it? Fareed asks him at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland.
On GPS: Fareed asks Israel’s President if he will pardon Netanyahu
But the saga began earlier. Police said there was sufficient evidence to indict Netanyahu in February 2018.
From the beginning, Netanyahu proclaimed his innocence, deriding the prosecution as a political witch hunt.
Last December, Netanyahu formally requested a pardon . In a letter to Israeli President Isaac Herzog, he said the trial had become “a focal point of fierce controversy” for which he bears “broad public and more responsibility, with an understanding of the overall ramifications of these events.” In the one-page letter, Netanyahu did not admit guilt or commit to anything about his political future.
One month earlier, Trump wrote his own letter to Herzog asking him to grant Netanyahu a full pardon.
“While I absolutely respect the independence of the Israeli Justice System, and its requirements, I believe that the ‘case’ against Bibi, who has fought alongside me for a long time, including against the very tough adversary of Israel, Iran, is a political, unjustified prosecution,” Trump wrote in the letter.
In Israel, only the president has the authority to issue a pardon.
Netanyahu’s main rivals, who seek to oust him after the election in late October, have yet to issue a statement following the court hearing.
Max Saltman in New York contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Investors led by U.S. billionaire Todd Boehly to buy Lukoil's oil and gas assets outside Russia, sources say
articles.title_zh: Investors led by U.S. billionaire Todd Boehly to buy Lukoil's oil and gas assets outside Russia, sources say
articles.content_orig:
Investors led by U.S. billionaire Todd Boehly's asset management company Eldridge have struck a deal to buy Lukoil's assets outside of Russia, sources confirmed to CNBC.
The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation and Catena Investments, based in the United Arab Emirates, are also parties to the deal, the sources said.
The deal transfers Lukoil's international refineries and other production assets in Bulgaria, Romania, Africa and the Middle East to the U.S.-led group, the sources said. It also includes retail gas stations in the U.S., Europe and Asia, they said.
The U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control is expected to sign off on the deal but final approval is still needed, the sources said. The deal would give the U.S.-led group about 350,000 barrels per day of production.
The agreement would allow Europe to buy fuel such as diesel previously produced by Lukoil through the U.S.-led group rather than Russia.

articles.title_orig: Young Britons’ sex lives have fallen off a cliff, major survey shows
articles.title_zh: Young Britons’ sex lives have fallen off a cliff, major survey shows
articles.content_orig:
Young Britons are having half as much sex as they were in 1990, according to a new study, with the average reported frequency falling from four times a month to just twice a month.
The data was produced as part of a long-running study known as the National Survey of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal), according to a statement Wednesday from the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM), which participates in the research.
“The sex lives of people in Britain have changed markedly since 1990 and they have substantial and varied sexual and reproductive health needs,” LSHTM said.
Researchers randomly selected around 6,700 people from England, Scotland and Wales aged 16-59 to participate in interviews and online surveys between September 2022 and January 2024.
This is the fourth edition of “one of the largest studies of sexual behaviour in the world,” which has previously been undertaken in 1990, 2000 and 2010.
In addition to adults under 45 years old reporting that they are having sex half as much as their peers did in 1990, the survey showed that 77% of 16-59-year-olds reported having sex in the past year, and 89% said they had sex at least once in their lives.
Among 16-24-year-olds, one in three said they had never had sex, up from around one in five in 2010.
Half of young women reported watching pornography in the past 12 months, compared with nearly 90% of male respondents. This was the first time the survey had asked about the use of online pornography.
Attitudes toward children and contraception are also changing. While the use of hormonal contraception declined among young women, the proportion of women who report that they don’t want children has doubled in the past decade.
The survey also reveals important findings for preventing the spread of sexually transmitted infections (STIs), with more than one in four sexually experienced 16-24-year-olds with exclusively opposite-sex partners reporting behaviors that are associated with STI risk.
These include “having four or more partners or condomless sex with two or more partners in the past year or overlapping partners in the past five years,” the statement said.
Men’s sexual health can predict heart issues
“While most adults are having sex, people are having sex less often and more young people have never had sex,” Soazig Clifton, academic director for Natsal at University College London, which also participates in the survey, said in the statement.
“There is also a higher proportion of people reporting same-sex experiences, and online sexual activity is now part of everyday life for many.”
Dr Otilia Mårdh, a scientific officer at the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC), who was not involved in the research, said that “another notable Natsal-4 finding is, that the proportion of men reporting both same-sex and opposite-sex partners (MSWM) more than doubled, from 0.9% (Natsal-3) to 2.3%.”
Feeling like a late bloomer when it comes to sex? There’s hope
“The authors note that this growing population could increasingly bridge sexual networks with different STI risks,” Mårdh said in a comment published by the Science Media Centre on Wednesday.
She added that this is “particularly relevant” as surveillance data from European monitoring programs shows “recent increases in syphilis and gonorrhoea among heterosexual populations, alongside rising congenital syphilis — contrasting with historically lower levels.”
“These trends highlight the need for accessible, stigma-free sexual health services offering prevention and testing tailored to people’s needs,” said Mårdh.
Five papers drawing on the results of the survey were published in the journal The Lancet.

articles.title_orig: South African President Wins Reprieve From ‘Farmgate’ Impeachment Investigation
articles.title_zh: South African President Wins Reprieve From ‘Farmgate’ Impeachment Investigation
articles.content_orig:
South African President Cyril Ramaphosa has won a legal battle to overturn a report that found he may have a case to answer over the theft of large sums of cash from his private farm.
In 2022, an independent panel said Ramaphosa may have committed serious misconduct relating to the theft of $580,000 (£443,000), hidden in a sofa, at his Phala Phala game farm in the Limpopo province. He denied any wrongdoing.
Ramaphosa challenged the findings of the report in court after the Constitutional Court ruled that parliament had violated the constitution by blocking moves to impeach him.
The Western Cape high court ruled that the panel's report was unlawful and set it aside "in its entirety".
In its judgment, the court said the panel, appointed by parliament to investigate the allegations against Ramaphosa, had "misconstrued its function, the nature of the inquiry it was to conduct and the recommendation it was required to make".
"It went beyond its lawful remit ... and made several material errors of law. [Therefore] the report of the independent panel ... is declared unlawful and is reviewed and set aside in its entirety," Judge Nolwazi Mabindla-Boqwana said.
The court also declared unlawful the steps taken by parliament in relation to the report.
Political analyst Khanyi Magubane said the court ruling was a victory for Ramaphosa as it gave him "political and constitutional credibility".
She made it clear that the ruling was not a criminal finding on possible improper conduct at the farm but rather an indictment at the independent panel's report.
"[So] he does get significant reprieve ... but there will always be the shadow of the Phala Phala report," Magubane said.
The ruling effectively removes the basis for the parliamentary impeachment process against Ramaphosa, although opposition parties have indicated they intend to challenge the decision.
The scandal, dubbed "Farmgate" by local media, has has dogged Ramaphosa since it emerged in 2022, when former spy chief Arthur Fraser reported the matter to police in a dossier.
Fraser, an ally of former President Jacob Zuma, accused Ramaphosa of concealing the theft from the police and tax authorities.
The break-in took place in 2020, when thieves allegedly stole bundles of US dollar bills hidden inside a sofa at the farm.
Earlier this month, two people were found guilty of the theft.
Ramaphosa confirmed that a robbery had taken place but said the money had been from the legitimate sale of buffalo from his livestock business.
Several investigations cleared him of any wrongdoing, but parliament began an impeachment proceedings in 2022 and appointed an independent panel to investigate the allegations.
The panel made a series of damaging findings, including that there was "substantial doubt about the legitimacy of the source of the currency that was stolen".
It also concluded that Ramaphosa "has a case to answer".
Ramaphosa initially challenged the report in court but withdrew his application after parliament voted against adopting its findings.
He revived the legal challenge again in May this year after the Constitutional Court, the country's highest court , ruled that parliament had acted unconstitutionally by blocking moves to impeach him.
It ordered parliament to refer the report to an impeachment committee.
In his latest challenge, Ramaphosa argued that the panel had "misconceived its mandate, misjudged the information placed before it and misinterpreted the four charges advanced against me".
The Western Cape High Court's ruling could bring the current impeachment process to an end, unless parliament successfully challenges the decision.
If they do, and the appeal is successful, the parliamentary committee would be able to examine the charges against the president and make a recommendation.
If the committee recommends impeachment, parliament would have to vote on whether to remove him from office. This would require the support of at least two-thirds majority in parliament.
Ramaphosa's Africa National Congress (ANC) has enough parliamentary seats to block such a move.
He is the first president to face impeachment proceedings under the rules introduced in 2018.
Legal expert Professor Richard Calland told the BBC he had expected the court ruling, given what he termed as "fault lines" in the independent panel's report.
Calland said the court's findings now meant that the impeachment process was "dead in the water [and] cannot continue".
He said that any political party that wanted to revive it "would have to come up with a whole new basis" for this.
Calland said political parties who want to hold Ramaphosa accountable would likely seek to appeal the ruling but it was unlikely parliament would also do so.
"So, the president's political career is now free of the cloud of impeachment," he said.

articles.title_orig: A rising star in China is the latest victim of Xi’s purge
articles.title_zh: A rising star in China is the latest victim of Xi’s purge
articles.content_orig:
FILE - Chen Jining, Communist Party Secretary for Shanghai attends a deliberation on the government work report, on the sideline of the National People's Congress at the Beijing Hotel, March 6, 2025. Ng Han Guan/AP hide caption
BANGKOK — Chinese Communist Party authorities are investigating Shanghai party secretary Chen Jining for suspected violations of party discipline, China's anti-corruption watchdog said Tuesday.
The Politburo member is the latest senior official targeted in President Xi Jinping's long-running anti-corruption campaign, which has shown no signs of letting up in scope or depth.
Chen is under investigation by the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection. The brief announcement by China's Central Commission for Discipline Inspection provided no further details.
A statement released by the Shanghai city government said the Standing Committee of the Shanghai Committee of the CCP "expressed firm support" for the decision to investigate Chen.
The decision sent "a clear and powerful signal that the fight against corruption would continue without pause or retreat," but with "a firm determination to win," the statement said.
The investigation follows sweeping purges under Xi, who has emphasized greater party discipline. The Chinese leader has pursued an anti-corruption campaign for more than a decade, carrying out purges on a scale not seen since Mao Zedong's rule.
"The takedown again shows that Xi Jinping's anti-corruption campaign has no limits," Mingda Qiu, a senior analyst at Eurasia Group, said in an emailed statement. "This is the fourth Politburo member to fall, and the fourth sitting member brought down in the current cycle. The pattern is unprecedented."
The recent Politburo purges highlight how much Chinese politics depend on shifting circumstances, with even officials with qualities that Xi apparently valued being vulnerable to removal, said Joseph Torigian, a professor at American University based in Washington.
"On paper," they appear to be "individuals Xi would appreciate," Torigian said, but afterward, "we could easily come up with hypotheses for why he got rid of them."
Other Politburo members purged include Gen. Zhang Youxia and He Weidong, both senior members of the Central Military Commission, which oversees the armed forces, and Ma Xingrui, a provincial party secretary.
The post of Shanghai party secretary has traditionally been viewed as a stepping stone to China's top leadership. The country's former President Jiang Zemin, its current premier, Li Qiang, and Xi himself previously held the position.
Chen has served as Shanghai party secretary since 2022. He previously held senior positions in Beijing's municipal government and headed the Ministry of Environmental Protection.

articles.title_orig: Chicago-bound American Airlines flight diverted to Phoenix; Video shows man being restrained
articles.title_zh: Chicago-bound American Airlines flight diverted to Phoenix; Video shows man being restrained
articles.content_orig:
CHICAGO -- A Chicago-bound American Airlines flight was forced to make an emergency landing after there was an apparent altercation on board.
American Airlines flight 1494 was headed from San Diego when it was diverted to Phoenix.
Video shows a man struggling with flight attendants.
A passenger who witnessed the incident said others on board jumped into action to help.
"It was remarkable how quickly everyone sprang into action to restrain this man and the flight attendants were remarkably orderly and calm," passenger Sean Bennett said.
Bennett said the plane landed safely and no one on board was hurt.
The FAA said in a statement, "American Airlines Flight 1494 landed safely at Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport around 1 a.m. local time on Wednesday, Nov. 25, after the crew reported a passenger disturbance on board. The flight departed San Diego International Airport and was headed to Chicago O'Hare International Airport. The FAA will investigate."
American Airlines said in a statement, "American Airlines flight 1494 diverted to Phoenix (PHX) due to a disruptive customer. Upon arrival, law enforcement met the aircraft and assisted with deplaning the customer before the flight continued to its destination. The safety and security of our customers and team members is our top priority. We thank our team members for their professionalism and our customers for their assistance and under standing."
The Phoenix Police Department said in a statement, "On November 25, 2026, at approximately 1:00 a.m., a flight traveling from San Diego to Chicago diverted to Phoenix due to a passenger-related disturbance. According to preliminary information, the passenger left his assigned seat and moved to the front of the aircraft, where he repeatedly refused crew instructions to return to his seat and attempted to manipulate an aircraft door. Crew members and passengers restrained the individual until the aircraft landed safely at Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport.
"No injuries were reported among passengers or crew members. The passenger sustained a minor injury and was transported to the hospital for evaluation. The incident occurred while the aircraft was flying near the Arizona-California border south of Needles, California. The FBI was notified and will review the officer's reports. The flight was subsequently delayed while the airline addressed operational concerns.
"The incident remains under investigation."

Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and millions of players are happily exploring Leonida and getting into heaps of trouble with Jason and Lucia. However, it appears that the game's demand is absolutely frying some PS5 consoles.
Almost one week after the game's release, Twitch streamer 'shivjam' shared a clip from her most recent broadcast showing her PS5 crashing mid-game. The screen freezes as Jason gets on a bike with Lucia, turns pixelated and green before it fails.
"#GTA6 tonight fried my PS5," shivjam said on X , adding, "The GPU is done and the console is gone. rip."
Shivjam noted in a separate post that the PS5 crashed earlier during the same broadcast and thought the issue resolved until her console fully died. But why is it happening in the first place?
Many have suggested the PS5's physical state could have contributed to the GPU frying, but shivjam showed the inside of her console in a follow-up post, and it shows very minimal dust coating the fans.
#GTA6 tonight fried my PS5. The GPU is done and the console is gone 🫩 rip https://t.co/KhLf62Ql8W November 24, 2026
"It was kept in open space and I showed on stream it was in good condition and very minor dust," she said.
Players speculated that the sheer size and the game's graphical demands could have overheated the streamer's GPU, but for now it's unclear what the reasoning is.

Shortly after GTA 6 's launch, streamer 'JoJoJosiah_' also experienced an issue that caused his PS5 to catch fire. In the clip posted to X , he had paused the game, left the room, and returned to find his PS5 smoking profusely.
Thankfully, JoJoJosiah_ said he was fine after the incident, but had to take a break from streaming.
"Was playing GTA VI on stream but had to go poop," JoJoJosiah_ said. "Paused it and put on a sensory vid for my chat. PS5 started just smoking out its a** and now I need to get a replacement."
Was playing gta VI on stream but had to go poop. Paused it and put on a sensory vid for my chat

These appear to be isolated incidents, but it is troubling that other players on Reddit have also experienced crashes and overheating. For now, it seems Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S consoles haven't had any issues, and Rockstar Games hasn't released a statement on the matter at this time.
Elsewhere, Rockstar has explained why technical complexities mean its most ambitious game ever is capped at 30fps on PS5 and Xbox, and why 40fps isn't an option .

articles.title_orig: China's Hansoh Pharma strikes drug deal with Bayer unit worth nearly $3.3 billion
articles.title_zh: China's Hansoh Pharma strikes drug deal with Bayer unit worth nearly $3.3 billion
articles.content_orig:
China Southern Airlines said in a filing late Tuesday that its subsidiary Xiamen Airlines had agreed to purchase 50 Boeing 737-8 aircraft with a combined catalog price of approximately $7.4 billion.
The announcement comes after President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he expected China to purchase another 250 Boeing aircraft, following his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the APEC summit last week.
"By the way, I sold 250 Boeings to China, and I think they're going to do another 250," Trump said.
In May, China approved an initial purchase of 200 Boeing aircraft for Chinese airlines following Trump's visit to Beijing, marking the country's first commitment to purchase U.S.-made Boeing aircraft since 2017, according to the White House.
It was not immediately clear whether Xiamen Airlines' latest purchase was part of that commitment.
China Southern, which owns a 55% stake in Xiamen Airlines, said the actual purchase price would be lower than the combined list price because of discounts offered by Boeing. The company did not disclose the final purchase price, citing confidentiality provisions in the agreement.
The aircraft are scheduled to be delivered in batches between 2031 and 2034, with the purchase financed through a combination of internal funds and external financing, the filing showed. The transaction remains subject to shareholder and relevant Chinese government approvals.
China Southern said the purchase would support Xiamen Airlines' planned relocation to the new Xiamen Xiang'an International Airport and the expansion of its route network.
The agreement follows the group's recent purchase agreement for 137 Airbus A320neo - family aircraft, the filing showed. China Southern said sourcing aircraft from different manufacturers would help diversify its fleet and improve operational flexibility.
Other Asian carriers, including Philippine Airlines and Malaysia Aviation Group , have also announced Boeing aircraft orders this month.

articles.title_orig: Poland Asks NATO to Shoot Down Russian Missiles Over Ukraine
articles.title_zh: Poland Asks NATO to Shoot Down Russian Missiles Over Ukraine
articles.content_orig:
Fox News anchor Jon Scott reports on NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte warning the alliance will defend every inch of Polish territory after a suspected airspace breach by Russia on ‘Fox Report.’
Poland announced Tuesday it had renewed its push for a permanent U.S. military presence in the country after two Russian airspace incursions in four days, including one in which a Swedish fighter jet under NATO command was cleared to shoot down a Russian cruise missile but held its fire.
The latest incursion came overnight Nov. 24, when a Russian drone briefly entered Polish airspace during attacks on Ukraine, four days after three Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles had crossed into Poland, prompting NATO to scramble fighter jets and bolster air defenses along its eastern flank.
Poland's chargé d'affaires in Washington, Bogdan Klich, said Tuesday that he briefed the White House National Security Council on the violations and renewed Warsaw's call to permanently station American troops in the NATO member country.
US URGES AMERICANS IN HISTORIC REGION TO STAY ALERT AFTER 'DANGEROUS' AIRSPACE INCIDENT
"Yesterday, I briefed the U.S. National Security Council on the violation of Polish airspace by Russian Kh-101 missiles and once again discussed the issue of the permanent deployment of U.S. troops in Poland," Klich wrote on X .
The new diplomatic push follows the incidents involving Russian assets and heightened concerns that Moscow's war in Ukraine will spill into NATO territory .
The Nov. 20 incursion involved a Swedish JAS 39 Gripen pilot operating under NATO command who was authorized to engage a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile, according to Lt. Gen. Ireneusz Nowak, commander of Poland’s Armed Forces Operational Command, as reported by The Kyiv Independent .
NATO's Combined Air Operations Centre in Uedem, Germany, issued conditional authorization to fire, but the pilot could not positively identify the object visually or through the aircraft's onboard electro-optical systems because of severe weather, Nowak said. No weapons were fired.
SUPERSONIC RUSSIAN JETS TRIGGER JOINT SCRAMBLE BY NATO ALLIES AMID PUTIN 'CLOWNS' JAB
Russian President Vladimir Putin chairs a meeting aboard the missile cruiser Varyag in Russia's far eastern Sakhalin region Aug. 12, 2026. Putin previously said Russia is not waging a sabotage campaign against Europe. (Reuters/File)
Polish authorities monitored 11 potentially threatening aerial objects during the attack, three of which entered the country's airspace, according to Nowak.
The Swedish Armed Forces said its jets had tracked several unidentified objects over Poland during the mission, which lasted several hours under difficult weather conditions.
Polish F-16 fighter jets, a Swedish Saab 340 early warning aircraft, a Dutch aerial refueling aircraft and ground-based air defense systems were also supporting the operation.
Polish prosecutors confirmed Sunday that debris recovered at three locations belonged to Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles, revising an initial military assessment that one of the objects might have been a drone, according to reports .
RUSSIA PREPARING HYBRID ATTACKS ON NATO'S EASTERN FLANK, INTELLIGENCE WARNS
His warning comes as NATO confronts a series of airspace violations, drone incidents and hybrid activity along its eastern flank. NATO’s military leadership said Friday that Russia’s actions continue to "test Allied resolve." (Olena Bartienieva/Getty Images)
Preliminary findings indicated the missiles were manufactured in October or November 2026 at a factory in Dubna in Russia's Moscow region, prosecutors said.
The second incursion happened overnight Nov. 24, when a Russian drone entered Polish airspace from Ukraine during another wave of Russian strikes on Ukraine.
Polish forces tracked the unmanned aircraft and received authorization to shoot it down but did not fire after it changed course and headed east, citing potential risks to civilians and property on the ground.
Deputy Defense Minister Paweł Zalewski said Polish authorities believed the violation was deliberate.
"It's hard to imagine this being a coincidence, so we assume it was an intentional act," Zalewski told RMF FM, according to Reuters .
After an emergency meeting of the North Atlantic Council on Monday, Nov. 23, NATO's supreme allied commander in Europe went on to authorize the forward deployment of an Airborne Warning and Control System, or AWACS, aircraft to Poland .
NATO WARNS PUTIN COULD STRIKE BEFORE EUROPEAN ARMY RESPONDS, POINTS TO US AS MILITARY MODEL
Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski addresses a joint news conference at a meeting of the foreign ministers of the so-called Weimar Triangle of France, Germany and Poland with Ukraine's foreign minister in Warsaw Sept. 29, 2025 (Wojtek Radwanski/AFP via Getty Images)
"All Allies stand in full solidarity with Poland. NATO remains united, ready, and committed to defending against any threat," NATO spokesperson Allison Hart said on X and as Warsaw summoned Russia's ambassador, according to Reuters.
In September, Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski said U.S. and Polish officials were working toward an agreement that could accommodate up to 10,000 American troops .
Roughly 7,000 U.S. troops were stationed in Poland on a rotational basis at the time while a permanent installation would expand Washington's military commitment along NATO's eastern flank.
"We want the kind of U.S. presence that would reassure us but not be threatening to Russia," Sikorski said during a Council on Foreign Relations event in New York, Bloomberg reported.

articles.title_orig: Five Mexicans arrested in Nigeria over $227m meth lab
articles.title_zh: Five Mexicans arrested in Nigeria over $227m meth lab
articles.content_orig:
Five Mexican nationals and a Nigerian businessman have been arrested in Nigeria after authorities uncovered an industrial-scale methamphetamine laboratory, the country's drug enforcement agency says.
More than 1.5 tonnes of the highly addictive synthetic drug, commonly known as meth, was seized from the facility in the south-eastern state of Enugu. The haul included both finished drugs and meth still being produced.
The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) estimates the drugs are worth $227m (£173m).
It is the fourth industrial-scale meth laboratory with alleged links to Mexican drug cartels to have been discovered in Nigeria in recent months.
The Nigerian businessman, 63-year-old Chuks Enoch Ezeike, also known as "Over Size", is accused of setting up the laboratory and smuggling the five Mexicans into the country using forged Argentine, Colombian and Chilean passports.
The NDLEA identified the five as Oscar Ramos-Cardenas, who it described as the alleged leader of the group, Juan Antonio Sarabia-Cabrera, Luis Enrique Garcia-Amador, Jose Alejandro Renteria-Reyes and Salomon Cabanillas-Torres.
The laboratory, situated behind an oil company in Enugu, also had accommodation for the Mexican nationals, allowing them to live and work there without attracting attention, the agency said.
Speaking at a news conference in the capital, Abuja, on Wednesday, NDLEA chief Mohamed Buba Marwa said the arrests followed a seven-month investigation involving several countries.
The agency had been monitoring Ezeike since April, when it received intelligence allegedly linking him to Ramos-Cardenas, a Mexican national suspected of specialising in large-scale meth production.
In August, the five Mexicans were refused entry into Nigeria after arriving at Abuja's international airport and were sent back to Mexico.
But less than a month later, they tried again, travelling through Colombia and France before arriving in neighbouring Benin, where they were allegedly given forged passports.
This time, Nigerian authorities deliberately allowed them into the country, Marwa said.
"We wanted the whole network: the meth specialist, the financier, the factory and the product. Sending them home a second time would only have postponed the problem," he said.
The men were allegedly met by Ezeike in Lagos before being taken to Enugu, where they were kept under surveillance.
More than 200 anti-narcotics officers were deployed on 11 November to raid the laboratory and a hotel where Ezeike was staying in simultaneous operations.
The five Mexicans were arrested while producing the drug, the agency said. Ezeike told investigators they had been due to leave Nigeria two days later.
Nearly seven tonnes of chemicals used to manufacture meth, as well as industrial equipment, were also seized.
The NDLEA said Ezeike had admitted owning the laboratory and bringing the Mexican nationals into Nigeria to produce the drug.
Investigators believe the operation was part of a wider international criminal network in which a Mexican cartel recruited and paid specialists to manufacture meth, while Nigerian collaborators allegedly provided the facilities and resources.
The agency has not identified the Mexican cartel it suspects was involved or said whether the six suspects have been formally charged.
The arrests come amid growing concerns about Mexican drug cartels setting up production bases in West Africa, a region long used as a transit route for illicit drugs.
While some of the meth produced in the region supplies a growing local market, traffickers also target lucrative overseas markets, particularly in Europe and Asia.
Earlier this year, Nigerian authorities uncovered similar laboratories in Ogun, Oyo and Ebonyi states.
The latest operation brings to 10 the number of suspected Mexican meth production specialists arrested in Nigeria in recent months, according to the NDLEA. Five others arrested in earlier operations are already in custody awaiting trial.
Issuing a warning to foreign drug cartels, Marwa said: "Nigeria is not your laboratory. It is not your warehouse, and it is not your transit route."

articles.title_orig: Five Russian military jets hit in airfield strike, says Ukraine
articles.title_zh: Five Russian military jets hit in airfield strike, says Ukraine
articles.content_orig:
A Russian MiG-31 military jet (file photo)
Ukraine has said it damaged five Russian military aircraft in an attack on Russia's Savasleyka airfield, 300km (185 miles) east of Moscow.
Three MiG-31 and two Su-34s aircraft were hit, Kyiv's General Staff said, adding that the extent of the damage was still being assessed but that "there may be even better news to come". It did not elaborate on what weapons it had used to hit the airfield.
Russia has not commented on the strikes.
The airfield at Savasleyka, in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region, has been a target for Ukraine for several years. It hosts aircraft used by Russia to launch hypersonic missiles and glide bombs.
The take-off of MiG-31s in particular frequently triggers nationwide alerts across Ukraine, as the Kinzhal missiles they carry have been known to hit large infrastructure and military targets and are difficult to shoot down.
Overnight, Kyiv also said it hit two oil refineries in Russia's Samara region some 800km (500 miles) from the front line â the latest in a series of long-range strikes which have dented Moscow's oil processing capacity.
"Did you repair them? We'll hit them again," the defence ministry in Kyiv said.
Samara region governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev said the night-time attacks had been "a true ordeal", with more than 145 drones shot down. One person was killed and several towns experienced power outages, Fedorishchev said.
Kyiv also said it had hit a radar system as well as fuel and logistics depots across Ukrainian territories currently occupied by Russia.
"Without fuel, military vehicles cannot move; without ammunition, artillery falls silent," the defence ministry said, adding that every successful hit meant Moscow could carry out fewer strikes.
Kyiv has developed a thriving weapons industry and Ukrainian strikes on Russian targets well beyond the front line have become commonplace in the years since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion.
On Tuesday, President Vladimir Putin called for a tightening of security measures across the country's energy facilities.
But he also argued that Russia had managed to stabilise its domestic fuel market without suffering "critical damage" and added that Moscow would "inevitably" retaliate against Kyiv.
Ukraine continues to come under daily attack. Ten people were killed across several regions between 24 and 25 November, while thousands are without power after Russian strikes on energy infrastructure.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia, AMD, and Micron stocks sink as investors flee AI trade
articles.title_zh: Nvidia, AMD, and Micron stocks sink as investors flee AI trade
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Nvidia ( NVDA ) stock retreated another 8% on Wednesday, following a 6% decline in the prior session as chip stocks continued to plunge amid a broader market sell-off.
Peers AMD ( AMD ) and Broadcom ( AVGO ) also extended losses from the prior session.
This year's once-hot AI trades continue to tumble, with memory chipmaker Micron Technology ( MU ) and peer SK Hynix ( SKHY ) tanking 11% and 8% respectively. Micron is more than 50% off its all-time high over the summer.
Storage and memory players Seagate (STX ), Western Digital ( WDC ), and Sandisk ( SNDK ) all fell on Wednesday. Sandisk, which recently implemented a stock split, is down roughly 70% from its June record high.
The violent move follows a stunning rally on Monday when Nvidia jumped 31% after the AI chip giant's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. But some strategists say tighter financial conditions and lingering questions around the AI trade are weighing on sentiment.
"There is still a lot of nervousness out there, and some investors have taken advantage of Monday's jump to cut their exposure to the AI trade," said David Morrison, senior market analyst at Trade Nation, on Wednesday.
He also noted the prevailing view that Huang is the only person who can hold the AI trade together "reeks of desperation," while investors increasingly perceive that "Nvidia's board is not the one that the world's leading chip designer should want."
Other areas of the AI trade retreated on Wednesday, including the stocks of neocloud providers CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and Nebius ( NBIS ), which each dropped by double-digit percentages.

articles.title_orig: Fed's preferred gauge of inflation climbs ahead of possible rate hike - ABC News
articles.title_zh: Fed's preferred gauge of inflation climbs ahead of possible rate hike - ABC News
articles.source: Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
articles.content_orig:
The Fed will issue a decision on interest rates early next month.
The Federal Reserve's preferred gauge of inflation climbed in October, according to a government report issued on Wednesday. The measure is sure to draw attention from central bankers as they weigh a possible rate increase early next month.
The Personal Consumption Expenditures price index (PCE) showed annual inflation climbed from 3.6% in September to 3.8% in October. The reading matched economists' expectations.
That figure for October marked the highest annual PCE in five months, putting inflation nearly two percentage points above the Fed's target level of 2%.
The report arrived weeks after a separate inflation measure, the Consumer Price Index (CPI), showed a larger jump in prices in October than economists had expected.
Fuel prices have accounted for a sizable share of overall inflation since the outbreak of the Iran war in late February set off a global oil supply shortage.
A cooldown in oil prices since the midterm elections has put downward pressure on gasoline prices, however, leaving the national average price of a gallon of gas at $3.58 as of Wednesday, AAA data showed. That figure amounted to a decline of about 15% from a month earlier.
The relief at the pump in recent weeks did not appear in the report on Wednesday, since it detailed prices in October.
The fresh data is sure to garner attention from the Fed at a delicate moment, when policymakers are weighing a rate increase that could help tackle inflation but risks a slowdown in hiring.
A stronger-than-expected jobs report earlier this month may ease possible concern among central bankers about a cooldown for the labor market.
Economic growth has also proven resilient, displaying better-than-expected performance in a quarterly report on gross domestic product released last month.
If the Fed were to issue a rate increase at its next meeting in December, the decision would mark the central bank's second rate hike in four months, after it had gone three years without raising rates.
The odds of a quarter-point rate hike at the Fed's next meeting are pegged at about 97%, according to CME Group's FedWatch Tool , a measure of market sentiment.
Days before the midterm elections, Fed policymakers opted to hold interest rates steady as they awaited further economic data. Still, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh vowed to cool off inflation.
"It’s our responsibility to get inflation down," Warsh said at a press conference in Washington, D.C., at the time.
Wall Street will also take notice of the PCE report after a volatile stretch of trading. The major stock indexes were mixed on Tuesday after soaring a day earlier in response to an announcement from Nvidia reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO.
Those fluctuations followed a selloff last week as tech investors digested fallout from Huang's previous resignation as well as an initial public offering from artificial intelligence giant Anthropic.

articles.title_orig: Inside Trump's effort to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO
articles.title_zh: Inside Trump's effort to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO
articles.content_orig:
Washington — Revelations that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an extramarital affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese intelligence asset have put the leading AI company under a microscope, as lawmakers and states question whether Nvidia skirted federal export rules that aim to stop its most advanced chips from going to China.
While Huang initially resigned his post amid scrutiny of his relationship with Alice Huang , a former executive at the Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed, Nvidia's board of directors announced Monday that it reinstated Huang as president and CEO .
News of Huang's return to Nvidia sent shockwaves through the business and political worlds, even as President Trump said he had spoken to the board and "convinced them" to bring Huang back. The president told CNBC in an interview that his administration gave Nvidia "assurances" that Huang is not a threat to national security.
The company, meanwhile, said it received "input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk."
Still, investigations by at least one state and Congress are unlikely to be derailed by Huang's dramatic return to Nvidia.
California Attorney General Rob Bonta served an investigative subpoena to Nvidia last week following revelations of Huang's affair with the woman who is alleged to have ties to China's Ministry of State Security.
Bonta, a Democrat, said the state's Department of Justice is seeking information from Nvidia about whether its advanced chips or confidential information may have gone to China and whether the company misled investors and the public.
"The conduct of Nvidia and its former CEO raises bright red flags, including about the ways in which the company may have misled investors," he said in a statement. "My office is investigating whether Nvidia or Jensen Huang's actions resulted in China obtaining advanced chips or confidential information — and if Nvidia misled investors and the public about this risk, in violation of the law."
Bonta said the information his office receives from Nvidia will help determine whether the company broke state law.
Numerous congressional committees were readying investigations into Huang's relationship with the alleged Chinese spy, and his reinstatement as CEO did not diminish lawmakers' appetite for more information about Huang's actions and whether his company's chips were diverted to China.
Huang is set to answer questions behind closed doors from lawmakers on three House panels, the Intelligence, Foreign Affairs and China Select Committee, on Dec. 1. Nvidia's general counsel, Tim Teter, will appear before the committees on Dec. 2.
The Senate Banking Committee will then hold a public hearing with Huang on Dec. 3.
Democrats, who will take control of the House and Senate in January, say they intend to launch investigations into Nvidia and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, whose agency oversees government export controls on sensitive technology.
House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, who is expected to serve as House speaker in the next Congress, denounced the decision by Nvidia's board to reinstate Huang as "indefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible."
"Congress will not be deterred from conducting a swift, thorough and wide-ranging investigation into business malfeasance by NVIDIA and corrupt abuse of power by Howard Lutnick and the Department of Commerce," he said in a statement Monday.
Senate Democrats have also pledged to act.
"Trump is putting his own financial interests and the needs of his billionaire buddies before our national security, emphasizing that he's learned nothing from his resounding election defeat," Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer wrote on X. "Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other NVIDIA executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain."
Sen. Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts, who is poised to take the helm of the Senate Banking Committee in January, said Nvidia officials and the Trump administration will have to answer questions from lawmakers.
"The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," she said in a statement. "The Trump Administration also needs to explain to Congress what 'input' was given and by which senior officials in the United States government to support his reinstatement."
House and Senate Democrats have also demanded that the president and his administration provide information about their role in Huang's reinstatement.
"President Trump has acknowledged personally intervening on Huang's behalf, and Nvidia has acknowledged that it received 'input from senior levels of the United States government' in reaching its decision," a group of five Democratic senators said in a joint statement. "The American people deserve to know why the president intervened in this extraordinary manner, whether serious counterintelligence or national security concerns were disregarded, and whose interests this intervention was intended to serve."
The senators are: Warren, Chris Coons of Delaware, Ron Wyden of Oregon, Jack Reed of Rhode Island and Maria Cantwell of Washington.
The Justice Department and Commerce Department said in a joint statement earlier this month that the federal government had been investigating Megaspeed, the Singapore-based computing company that is a Nvidia client, since 2024.
The Commerce Department sought records from Nvidia in May 2025 about direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed and placed the Singaporean company on its "no sell" list that June.
Agents with the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, working with Singaporean law enforcement, conducted an on-site, in-person check at Megaspeed in June 2025 and interviewed Alice Huang, the Commerce and Justice Departments said in their statement. After that action, the Justice Department took the lead in the criminal probe into Megaspeed.
Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing and said Alice Huang left the company in August 2025. China has denied allegations that she is a spy.
Mr. Trump told reporters earlier this month that the FBI was "looking into" Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, who is of no relation. A Justice Department official said Monday that Attorney General Todd Blanche spoke with Mr. Trump about Jensen Huang and Nvidia over the weekend, and said "the DOJ has no evidence of any wrongdoing" by either Huang or his company.
At a press conference Tuesday, the attorney general said the Justice Department did not have any information showing Huang committed criminal acts, and if he had, Blanche "would have certainly told the president."
Reporters pressed Blanche on how he and the Justice Department had made that determination if there was no investigation into Alice Huang or potential violations of federal export control laws by Nvidia. He dodged questions on the topic. Still, the attorney general referred to Nvidia as a "good corporate citizen."
Blanche said that "looking into it" does not mean there was an investigation into the Nvidia CEO and his alleged mistress, or the company itself.
The attorney general also said there was a "collective consensus" to conclude there was no national security risk posed by Huang.
The Securities and Exchange Commission is conducting its own civil investigation into Nvidia, the Wall Street Journal reported last week. Among the matters that the SEC will look into is whether the company's disclosures misled investors, sources told the Journal.
The Wall Street Journal reported on Nov. 11 that Nvidia altered its reporting methods for international chip sales and stopped reporting revenue tied to Singapore on financial disclosures last year.

articles.title_orig: U.S. plans to hike tariffs on China, EU, Brazil and others over subsidized production
articles.title_zh: U.S. plans to hike tariffs on China, EU, Brazil and others over subsidized production
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump's administration is getting ready to raise tariffs on China, the European Union and a dozen other trading partners
WASHINGTON -- President Donald Trump's administration is planning to hike tariffs on Chinese goods by an additional 20% and raise import taxes on products from the European Union, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and nine other major trading partners.
The new tariffs are meant to discourage excessive manufacturing output in those economies, boosted by subsidies and other trade barriers that the Republican administration says put American manufacturers at a disadvantage. The taxes are also intended to help replace the tariff revenues lost after the Supreme Court ruled in February that Trump could not declare an economic emergency to bypass Congress and impose across-the-board tariffs.
In a late-night call with reporters on Tuesday, a senior administration official provided details of the planned tariffs ahead of the release of a series of investigations into the trade practices of 12 countries, the 27-member EU and the self-governing island of Taiwan. The official insisted on anonymity as a condition for discussing the reports before they were posted by the U.S. Trade Representative's office.
The official stressed that the tariffs were still at the proposal stage and did not provide strict timelines on possible implementation.
The tariffs — rolled out early Wednesday, the day before Thanksgiving — represent another controversial twist in Trump's economic policy. Voters in this month's midterm elections punished Republicans by handing majorities in the House and the Senate to Democrats, with about two-thirds of voters saying that Trump's policies had made the economy worse, according to The AP Voter Poll , a sweeping survey of the American electorate conducted in all 50 states.
Trump has promised that the import taxes will bring back manufacturing jobs and reduce the federal deficit, but last year's tariffs contributed to higher inflation that angered voters and led to calls by Democratic lawmakers to require congressional approval going forward.
The Trump administration argues that these countries have helped spur an influx of goods at lower prices that undercut American companies, creating a trade deficit in goods that has recently exceeded $1 trillion annually.
The legal basis of the planned tariffs is Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which enables the U.S. government to investigate and retaliate against foreign trade practices that violate existing deals, are not justified by market forces or actively discriminate against American goods. The official told reporters that the new tariffs would be consistent with the trade deals that Trump reached last year with dozens of countries after threatening severe tariff hikes .
Brazil was singled out for extra punishment after talks on trade issues stalled, the official said. The U.S. is proposing higher import taxes for raw and refined sugar and a new 10% tariff on aircraft, a move that would hit Embraer, Brazil’s largest aircraft maker.
For some Chinese goods, the new 20% tariff will be stacked on top of other import taxes for a total rate of 45%.
The U.S. and China reached a trade truce last year that is set to expire on Jan. 10. The new tariffs will not come as a surprise to Beijing and are unlikely to undermine the truce, the administration official said.
Trump met last week in Shenzhen, China, with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and plans to host him next month at the Group of 20 summit in Florida, an event at which the truce and issues over access to rare earth minerals and China's purchases of American agricultural products could be discussed again.
The official stressed that the tariffs are targeted to specific products. They would not stack on top of separate tariffs on automobiles, steel, aluminum and other products that the administration has separately imposed under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962.
Neither will they stack on top of levies of 10% to 12.5% announced in July for 60 trading partners that the White House said have inadequately enforced bans on goods produced by forced labor.
Other nations facing the new tariffs are Bangladesh, Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Thailand and Vietnam. The official said there are two other countries with pending investigations: Mexico and Norway.
The Associated Press confirmed the planned tariff announcement ahead of the call, according to people who insisted on anonymity because they were not authorized to comment publicly. The plans were reported earlier on Tuesday by Bloomberg and The Wall Street Journal.

articles.title_zh: Gold Holds Decline as US Tariff Plans Reinforce Rate-Hike Bets
articles.content_orig:
Kitco NEWS has a diverse team of journalists reporting on the economy, stock markets, commodities, cryptocurrencies, mining and metals with accuracy and objectivity. Our goal is to help people make informed market decisions through in-depth reporting, daily market roundups, interviews with prominent industry figures, comprehensive coverage (often exclusive) of important industry events and analyses of market-affecting developments.
(Kitco News) - The gold market continues to struggle to attract consistent bullish momentum as expectations that the Federal Reserve will maintain its hawkish monetary policies into the new year have driven real yields and the U.S. dollar higher, increasing the opportunity cost of holding a non-yielding asset.
However, Iggy Ioppe, Chief Investment Officer of Theo Network, a financial and tokenization platform, said that while gold has room to move lower in the near term, investors shouldn’t ignore the long-term, real-world value of holding the precious metal.
He added that while most investors are familiar with the old commodity market cliché that “the cure for high commodity prices is high prices,” the opposite is also true, especially when it comes to gold.
“The cure for low gold prices is low gold prices,” he said in an interview with Kitco News.
Ioppe explained that he divides the gold market into two distinct groups: momentum-driven investors, who amplify price movements, and self-correcting buyers, who become increasingly active as prices fall.
Although momentum-driven investors currently dominate the market, Ioppe said that lower prices should eventually stimulate physical demand from central banks, jewelry consumers and retail investors.
He noted that some central banks operate with fixed budgets for their gold purchases, meaning they can accumulate more of the precious metal as prices fall. At the same time, lower prices should help revive jewelry demand in China and India, where consumers are particularly price-sensitive.
“The self-correcting buyers, that’s medium and long term. A lot of the amplifying momentum buyers, they’re clustered in the very short term,” he said.
Ioppe added that there could also be significant pent-up investment demand from investors who sat on the sidelines during gold’s historic rally. He noted that many of the Wall Street and Silicon Valley investors he speaks with still have no exposure to the precious metal.
Unlike equities, where a significant decline in share prices could reflect a fundamentally broken business model, Ioppe said that gold’s underlying value proposition remains intact despite its recent selloff.
“ Gold is going to, at the minimum, keep up with the purchasing power,” he said.
Although Ioppe is not ruling out further selling pressure in the gold market, he questioned how sustainable the current environment of elevated real yields is, given the U.S. government’s deteriorating fiscal position.
He noted that yields on 10-year Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities have risen to roughly 2.9%, up from 1.8% a year ago. According to his analysis, roughly two-thirds of that increase reflects expectations of tighter U.S. monetary policy, while the remaining third reflects growing concerns about the creditworthiness of the U.S. government.
While higher real yields make Treasuries more attractive than gold in the near term, Ioppe said that investors will eventually have to recognize that some of those higher returns are compensation for taking on additional sovereign debt risk.
“It kind of creates the illusion of yield in the near term,” he said. “But at some point, people realize that there is no yield if there is risk embedded in it.”
Ioppe also warned that bond markets could be overly optimistic about the Federal Reserve’s ability to bring inflation back down to its 2% target.
He explained that the central bank’s ability to withstand political pressure has strengthened its credibility with financial markets. However, growing global economic fragmentation and trade barriers remain significant structural inflationary forces.
Looking ahead, Ioppe said that weaker employment data, softer inflation readings or a more dovish Federal Reserve could provide the catalyst gold needs to reverse its current momentum.
He added that lower oil prices could also provide some relief for the precious metal. Along with easing inflation pressures, lower energy prices would leave major gold-consuming nations, particularly those dependent on energy imports, with more capital to purchase gold.
Ioppe said that a recovery in investment demand could be particularly powerful as momentum-driven investors are forced to cover their short positions while physical buyers continue to take advantage of lower prices.
Beyond gold’s traditional fundamental drivers, Ioppe sees significant long-term potential in the growing tokenization of the precious metal, particularly as the technology addresses one of gold’s biggest shortcomings as an investment asset: its lack of yield.
Theo Network has developed gold and silver products that generate returns by leasing physical precious metals to industry participants, including refiners.
Ioppe explained that jewelers, bullion dealers and other industry participants could benefit from borrowing directly in gold rather than borrowing U.S. dollars to finance their inventories.( Kitco Global Index shows how much of today's gold move is the dollar versus the gold market itself.)
Although this financing model does not necessarily increase industrial demand for gold, he said that it could generate incremental investment demand by allowing a greater portion of the world’s above-ground gold stocks to generate a return.
“If they borrow from people that have physical gold, like us, and pay the interest in gold, that means a bigger percentage of the gold out there actually starts to pay yield, and that’s what creates incremental demand for gold,” he said.
While the tokenized gold market remains relatively small compared with the broader precious metals market, Ioppe said that its growing utility gives it a significant long-term advantage over traditional gold-backed exchange-traded funds.
Although ETFs have made gold more accessible to investors, he said that tokenization takes the precious metal beyond its role as a passive investment, allowing it to function more effectively as a monetary asset.
Even without generating a yield, tokenized gold can facilitate payments and wealth transfers, allowing consumers to hold their savings in gold rather than fiat currencies.
“ETF is a start. It’s good for investment, which is only one aspect of it,” he said. “Tokenized gold has utility. You can send it, you can pay for things, you can send tiny amounts. It’s available 24/7.”

articles.title_orig: China’s Huawei Convicted in U.S. Over Bank Fraud, Iran Ties
articles.title_zh: China’s Huawei Convicted in U.S. Over Bank Fraud, Iran Ties
articles.content_orig:
China’s biggest technology firm and the world’s largest telecommunications equipment maker has been convicted in the U.S. of stealing trade secrets and defrauding banks about its business in Iran.
Huawei was found guilty on 10 of 12 counts by a jury in Brooklyn on Tuesday. The verdict all but brings to a close an almost eight-year-long criminal case against Huawei and three of its subsidiaries. The sprawling legal case spanned a 12-week trial, dozens of witnesses, and hundreds of motions and filings.
It’s a rare case of U.S. prosecutors securing a conviction against a foreign corporation and could have significant consequences for both Huawei and U.S.-China relations.
The Justice Department first announced charges against Huawei in January 2019 as part of the first-term Trump Administration’s “China Initiative,” a controversial program to investigate and prosecute Chinese influence and espionage in the U.S.
The Shenzhen-based tech giant was found guilty of bank and wire fraud, conspiracy to steal trade secrets, and violations of U.S. sanctions. It faces massive potential penalties, including fines, forfeiture, and restitution. Sentencing is set for September 2027, with motions in advance of sentencing expected to start in the third week of January.
“Few crimes are as serious as Huawei’s decades-long pattern of endangering U.S. national security, violating the sanctity of U.S. commerce, and impeding the enforcement of U.S. laws,” U.S. Attorney Joseph Nocella Jr. said .
James Barnacle Jr., assistant director in charge of the FBI’s New York office, added, “Huawei’s success was built on deception and theft, and the FBI will never hesitate to pursue those who profit by breaking the law.”
The jury, however, acquitted Huawei of the most serious charge: racketeering conspiracy under the Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organisations Act (RICO).
Huawei’s attorney Brian Heberlig argued that U.S. prosecutors “began with guilt and worked backwards,” basing their claims of conspiracy on isolated incidents.
Huawei’s success, he said, is “about competition, not conspiracy. Innovation, not theft. Ordinary business dealings, not criminal conduct.”
Heberlig told reporters that the company will appeal the case.
“We believe the government’s remaining charges are equally without legal or factual merit,” Huawei said in a statement . “We will thoroughly review the relevant verdicts and take all necessary legal actions to defend our rights and interests.”
Huawei lawyer Brian Heberlig speaks to reporters outside federal court in Brooklyn, N.Y., on Nov. 24, 2026. Larry Neumeister—AP
Huawei was convicted of conspiracy to steal trade secrets from U.S. companies over two decades. Its alleged theft includes router source code from Cisco Systems, semiconductor equipment from CNEX Labs, robotic phone testing equipment from T-Mobile, antenna technology from Quintel, and networking equipment information from Fujitsu Network Communications. The jury also found Huawei and its subsidiaries guilty of violating the International Emergency Economic Powers Act and money laundering.
During the trial, which began Sept. 8, the jury watched a video that prosecutors said showed a Huawei engineer unbolting and detaching the arm of a high-speed T-Mobile testing robot and slipping it into his backpack. The engineer said he found the piece in his bag, calling the incident a “mistake,” and returned it the next day after T-Mobile reported it missing, but not before a visiting engineer from China allegedly measured and photographed the robotic arm, according to prosecutors. Huawei later fired the employee.
Prosecutors also argued that Huawei had hired a professor to gain access to a circuit board developed by CNEX.
“Huawei cultivated a culture of crime and corruption, and that crime was an important business strategy,” U.S. prosecutor Taylor Stout said in his opening statement.
Huawei’s attorneys called 15 witnesses to give evidence that the company’s success came from its own innovation. The attorneys cited the company’s 110,000-person research and development team and its over 165,000 patents. Heberlig said prosecutors had “cherry-picked” instances of employee misconduct that were not representative of Huawei’s company culture.
Prosecutors also argued that Huawei deliberately deceived global banks, including HSBC, BNP Paribas, and Standard Chartered, about its business in Iran and North Korea, which are both subject to U.S. sanctions. Huawei allegedly presented its Iran subsidiary, Skycom Tech, as an independent entity to skirt sanctions.
The jury, however, rejected the government’s assertion that Huawei had conspired in a racketeering scheme to expand its global business. If the company had been convicted of the RICO charge, it could have faced potential forfeiture of parts of its enterprise.
“It’s hard not to have profoundly mixed emotions from the verdict we just heard,” Heberlig, Huawei’s attorney, told reporters. The RICO charge, he said, “alleged that the company was corrupt from top to bottom, that it had a corporate culture and policy of cheating, stealing, and lying, and the jury found the company not guilty on that charge.”
The jury also acquitted the company of conspiring to obstruct a federal grand jury investigation.
The legal case is among the most extensive against a corporation, involving millions of documents in evidence, covering source code, financial records, and emails. Jurors spent five days, beginning Nov. 18, deliberating the case.
“Rarely has a jury had to commit so much of their personal time to a trial,” U.S. District Judge Ann Donnelly, who oversaw the case, said.
The case also took a winding path before the trial even began. It was delayed for years during the COVID-19 pandemic. In 2022, U.S. prosecutors also charged two Chinese intelligence officers with trying to bribe a U.S. government employee with $61,000 in bitcoin to steal evidence and information about the case.
The case could have ramifications on the U.S.’s relationship with China. The verdict comes days after President Donald Trump met with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen. It also comes amid tensions over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy , which has renewed calls by U.S. lawmakers for tighter restrictions on A.I. chip sales to China .
Huawei, which is privately held, is one of China’s largest and most famous companies. The company reported 880.9 billion RMB ($126 billion) in revenue last year. It employs more than 200,000 employees globally and operates in more than 170 countries.
The case spawned a diplomatic crisis in 2018, when Canadian authorities detained Huawei Chief Financial Officer Meng Wanzhou, who is also the daughter of the company’s founder, at the U.S.’s request. Meng had been secretly indicted on U.S. charges of bank and wire fraud.
Meng pleaded not guilty to criminal charges and fought extradition to the U.S. while under house arrest in Vancouver for nearly three years. She entered a deferred prosecution agreement in 2021, which acknowledged that she had misled an HSBC banker about Huawei’s relationship with Skycom, after which she returned to China. A federal judge dismissed the charges against her with prejudice in December 2022. The HSBC executive Meng had met with in 2013 testified in the Brooklyn trial.
The first charges were announced as Washington and Beijing were locked in a trade war.
Since the first-term Trump Administration launched the “China Initiative” in 2018, federal prosecutors have secured convictions against a number of foreign nationals, but corporate cases have had mixed outcomes. Taiwan’s United Microelectronics pleaded guilty to stealing trade secrets in 2020, and China’s Hytera Communications pleaded guilty to conspiring to steal trade secrets in 2025. Chinese chipmaker Fujian Jinhua was acquitted in 2024. A separate federal case in Seattle against two Huawei subsidiaries has been repeatedly delayed, with a trial date set for October

articles.content_orig:
This is read by an automated voice. Please report any issues or inconsistencies here .
See more from the L.A. Times in Google Search. Set us as preferred
SHENZHEN, China — President Trump has begun an extraordinary visit to Shenzhen, where he is set to join the leaders of Russia and China — two of Washington’s principal geopolitical rivals — for an unprecedented trilateral summit Thursday.
Chinese President Xi Jinping personally welcomed Trump on the tarmac upon his arrival, reciprocating a rare honor Trump extended to him during his September visit to Washington.
All three leaders attended a dinner alongside other regional heads of government on Wednesday night, participating in the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, known as APEC.
The trilateral meeting will be the first of its kind by leaders of the United States, Russia and China, three nations with the world’s largest nuclear arsenals.
But while Trump has embraced a strategy of diplomatic engagement with historic foes, the three leaders enter the meeting with starkly different agendas.
Russian President Vladimir Putin hopes to secure space and time to continue executing his war against Ukraine. Trump says he would like to discuss a nuclear arms control agreement and his war in Iran. And Xi aims to present China as a superpower on the international stage, capable of forging world peace.
Meeting with Putin before Trump arrived, Xi said that China’s relationship with Russia had remained as steadfast “as a rock through wind and rain.”
The two sides, he said, would pursue a “multipolar world” — a vision for a global balance of power that would see American influence weakened across Europe and Asia.
A new rule tightening loopholes in U.S. export controls sends a dual message to Beijing ahead of Thursday’s summit.
Trump, for his part, has hedged on his expectations of the summit, signaling resolve against China ahead of his arrival here.
On Monday, the Trump administration tightened export controls on semiconductor chips essential to artificial intelligence development, closing loopholes aimed at curbing Chinese efforts to circumvent restrictions — a move that Trump acknowledged might be an “insult” to Xi before the meeting.
Chinese officials said Wednesday afternoon that Beijing reserved the right to retaliate.
“In essence, the United States is simultaneously trying to find limited avenues of cooperation with China while trying to clamp down on their access to critical parts of the AI supply chain, which doesn’t set up the conditions for productive dialogue,” said Aalok Mehta, director of the Wadhwani AI Center at the Center for Strategic and International Studies.
Trump also met in Manila on Tuesday with fellow members of the Quad — India, Japan and Australia — in a show of resolve toward Beijing.
“Our countries are the four corners of a free, open, stable, and prosperous Indo-Pacific,” Trump said in the Philippines.
“We continue to protect peace through strength,” he added.
